subject: humanities
passage: Many railway stations in Europe now have public pianos that anyone may play. Musicologist Elena Varga counted how many people played the pianos at two stations in Budapest, Hungary: one used mainly by commuters and one used mainly by tourists. She found that at the commuter station, people seem to avoid playing when the station is most crowded: ______

data.title: People Playing Public Pianos at Two Budapest Stations

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?

choices.A: at the commuter station, only 2 to 4 people played per hour at 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., but 11 to 14 at midday.
choices.B: at the commuter station, the piano was played by 9 people per hour at 7 p.m., more than at 5 p.m.
choices.C: at the tourist station, the number of players stayed between 9 and 12 per hour throughout the day.
choices.D: at the commuter station, more people played the piano at 5 p.m. than at any other time of the day.

explanation.why: The statement says commuter-station players avoid the busiest times. For a commuter station, the busiest times are the morning and evening rush hours, so the choice must compare those hours with quieter ones. The commuter line drops to 2 to 4 players at 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. and rises to 11 to 14 at midday.
explanation.A: Correct. Playing dropped sharply during the morning and evening rush hours and peaked in the quieter middle of the day.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true, but comparing two evening hours does not show that players avoid both rush hours compared with quieter times.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true, but it describes the tourist station, not the commuter station the statement is about.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The graph shows only 4 players at 5 p.m. at the commuter station, one of its lowest values, not its highest.
